responses.sql: SELECT rating, AVG(length) AS avg_length, AVG(rental_rate / rental_duration) AS avg_rate_per_duration_day FROM film WHERE replacement_cost > 20.99 GROUP BY rating;

assumptions.assumption: 'Expensive' means replacement_cost strictly greater than 20.99 (cutoff itself excluded). Since replacement_cost takes values like 19.99 and 22.99 ending in .99, no film sits exactly at 20.99, so > and >= give the same result.

The average of rental_rate / rental_duration is computed per film (ratio for each film, then averaged), not as a ratio of sums. rental_duration is NOT NULL and at least 3, so there are no divide-by-zero concerns.

responses.sql: SELECT rating, AVG(length) AS avg_length, AVG(rental_rate / rental_duration) AS avg_rate_per_day FROM film WHERE replacement_cost > 20.99 GROUP BY rating

assumptions.assumption: 'Expensive' means replacement_cost strictly greater than 20.99 (the cutoff itself is excluded). Since costs are in 0.01 steps ending in .99, the cutoff value 20.99 is an actual value, so >= would differ.
AVG(length) ignores NULL lengths by default, and the per-film ratio rental_rate / rental_duration is averaged per film; rental_duration is NOT NULL with values 3-7, so there is no division by zero.

alternatives.interpretation: Expensive means replacement_cost at or above 20.99 (cutoff inclusive).
